pathway.title: Karman Holdings Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is average to strong, because sole- and single-source positions on long-lived programs and a rising order book give revenue visibility. Revenue grew 36.57% in 2025 and 54.85% in the first half of 2026, the company puts second-quarter organic growth at 24.4% without defining it, and backlog rose from USD 801,056 thousand at year-end 2025 to USD 1.3 billion at 30 June 2026. Programs can run for more than 20 years and the company says customers rarely requalify a supplier, so contracted work should convert into earnings that service debt, but the government may terminate contracts and its contracts are generally not fully funded at inception, so backlog measures visibility and not cash, and the company dropped the word funded from its backlog label in 2025 without restating amounts. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2025-09-30_ck0002040127-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2

Margins are stable on the company's adjusted measure and thinner on reported earnings, so leverage should be sized on the reported figure. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 29.16% in 2023, 30.74% in 2024, 30.82% in 2025 and 29.82% in the first half of 2026 against 30.48% a year earlier, while reported EBITDA margin was 27.16%, 28.39%, 25.41% and 26.30%. Add-backs of USD 25,476 thousand in 2025 were 17.53% of adjusted EBITDA and mostly acquisition costs and share-based compensation, and integration costs are still added back, so the adjusted margin is a less conservative measure of recurring cash earnings while the acquisition program continues. Gross margin rose from 37.60% in 2023 to 40.30% in 2025 and 42.64% in the first half of 2026, the clearest sign of operating leverage. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 8

Cash conversion is the weakest dimension, because EBITDA is not yet turning into free cash flow. Operating cash flow was negative USD 22,119 thousand in 2025 and negative USD 2,975 thousand in the first half of 2026, and free cash flow after capital expenditure, positive USD 11,393 thousand in 2024, was negative USD 42,455 thousand in 2025 and negative USD 24,840 thousand in the first half of 2026, a smaller outflow than the negative USD 39,624 thousand of the first half of 2025 and negative USD 27,671 thousand over the twelve months to 30 June 2026. Growth absorbs cash before it is billed: in the first half of 2026 receivables took USD 25,455 thousand and contract assets USD 24,851 thousand, and capital expenditure rose from 4.31% of revenue in 2025 to 6.56%. Debt, not cash flow, has therefore funded the acquisitions and the shortfall, and deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and on working capital turning. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4

Leverage is high for a company with negative free cash flow and was built faster than earnings. Net debt was USD 705,196 thousand at 30 June 2026, 4.47x reported EBITDA and 3.94x adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months, and finance leases of USD 102,139 thousand outside those figures take net leverage to 5.11x. Year-end 2025 net leverage was 3.88x on net debt of USD 465,189 thousand and, pro forma for the Seemann acquisition paid for on 3 February 2026, USD 675,189 thousand and 5.63x on earnings that hold none of the acquired business. If the 2026 outlook of USD 215.0 million to USD 222.5 million of adjusted EBITDA is met and net debt does not rise, net leverage would be 3.22x on that measure, but the outlook excludes any future acquisition. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C9; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing risk is low before 2030, but both rest on the revolver and on a floating-rate term loan. Cash of USD 51,741 thousand and the undrawn revolver of USD 150.0 million give liquidity of USD 201,741 thousand, which equals 4.06 years of the first-half free cash outflow at an annual pace, and 74.35% of it is the revolver. Only scheduled amortization falls due before the revolver matures in 2030 and the term loan on 1 April 2032, the term loan bore 6.46% at 30 June 2026, and the August 2026 amendment lowers the margin by 50 bp, worth about USD 3,820 thousand a year and lifting cash interest cover from 2.97x to 3.20x. The only financial covenant, 6.50x first-lien net leverage, applies when the revolver is drawn above a threshold the filings do not state, so headroom is not calculable. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25

Concentration in a few prime contractors limits diversification and ties earnings and receivables to the same counterparties. Three customers supplied 51.5% of revenue in 2025, two customers held 40.7% of receivables at year-end 2025 and 29.7% at 30 June 2026, and the company estimates that no single program exceeded 12% of revenue. Revenue is balanced across three end markets (31.81%, 31.78% and 36.41% in 2025) and a maritime end market added USD 59,970 thousand in the first half of 2026, but all of it rests on U.S. defense and space budgets, so a delay at one prime would hit earnings and cash collection together. Basis: calculation C12; calculation C15; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

Financial policy and governance are the open question: policy is acquisitive and unremediated control weaknesses leave reported figures provisional, while the record on distributions is creditor-friendly. Four acquisitions since April 2025 carried a combined fair value of consideration of USD 470,428 thousand, and a fifth, Walker, was agreed in July 2026 for about USD 94.0 million with its funding not described; no leverage target is stated. Management reports that internal control was not effective at year-end 2025 and at 30 June 2026, no dividend is planned and lenders accepted margin cuts of 75 bp and 50 bp, but who controls the company is not established because the proxy statement and the stockholder agreements are not supplied. Basis: calculation C14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 153–155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43

The sector backdrop supports demand but concentrates risk in U.S. government budgets. Management points to more than USD 90 billion of recent prime-contractor awards for interceptors and over USD 76 billion for submarines, and the annual report says its proven missile-defense programs are positioned to feed the Golden Dome program, yet it also warns of shutdowns and continuing resolutions, tariffs and tight skilled labor. Budget disruption would delay awards and cash receipts at the primes that supply 51.5% of revenue, which is why sector deterioration is a monitoring trigger. Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1

runs.text: Strength one is the sole- and single-source position on long-lived programs: the company holds such positions on many programs, programs can run for more than 20 years and requalification is costly, so revenue persists once a program is in production, which supports debt service across a downturn in any one end market. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17

Strength two is the order book: backlog of USD 801,056 thousand at year-end 2025 rose to USD 1.3 billion at 30 June 2026, about 2.21x twelve-month revenue, which gives visibility into the 2026 outlook and supports leverage coming down if conversion to revenue holds. Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_krmn-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2

Strength three is a stable adjusted EBITDA margin near 30%, with gross margin up from 37.60% in 2023 to 42.64% in the first half of 2026, so growth has so far added earnings at a steady margin that can carry interest of USD 53,144 thousand a year. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength four is liquidity and maturity: USD 201,741 thousand of liquidity, only scheduled amortization before 2030 and a term loan due 2032, which lets the company absorb the cash outflow for years without a refinancing. Basis: calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18

Weakness one is leverage built by acquisitions: net debt of USD 705,196 thousand is 4.47x reported EBITDA, four acquisitions with combined fair value of consideration of USD 470,428 thousand were completed in under one year and debt arrives before acquired earnings, so a shortfall in integration or growth lifts leverage quickly. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness two is negative free cash flow: negative USD 27,671 thousand over the twelve months, narrower than in 2025 but still negative, with contract assets and receivables absorbing cash ahead of billing, so debt service and growth are funded by borrowing and deleveraging depends on EBITDA alone. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4

Weakness three is customer concentration: three customers supplied 51.5% of revenue and two held 40.7% of receivables at year-end 2025, so one program decision moves earnings and collections together. Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10

Weakness four is reporting quality: management reports that internal control was not effective at year-end 2025 and at 30 June 2026, so interim figures that covenant tests and lenders use may be revised. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 153–155; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 41–43

Weakness five is that control and financial policy are not visible: no holder is named, no leverage target is stated and a pending acquisition has no described funding, so the willingness to protect creditors cannot be tested beyond the behavior to date. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The company completed its initial public offering in February 2025, selling 8.4 million of the 26.5 million shares at USD 22.00, and on 1 April 2025 replaced its earlier lender with a Citibank credit agreement made up of a USD 300.0 million term loan maturing in April 2032 and a USD 50.0 million revolver. New debt since then is the term loan increases, each tied to an acquisition: USD 75.0 million in May 2025 for ISP, USD 130.0 million in October 2025 for Five Axis and the revolver repayment, and USD 265.0 million in February 2026 for Seemann Composites and MSC. The revolver commitment was raised to USD 150.0 million in March 2026 and nothing was drawn in the first half of 2026. Basis: 10-Q_2025-09-30_ck0002040127-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108; 10-K_2025-12-31_krmn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18

Fair values of consideration were USD 82.3 million for MTI, USD 58.6 million for ISP, USD 96.6 million for Five Axis and USD 232.9 million for Seemann, together USD 470.4 million, and the Walker agreement of July 2026 for about USD 94.0 million is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 with funding not described. No bond or note issue appears in the documents; the new borrowing is under the one credit agreement, which is not itself supplied, and other notes payable were USD 4,516 thousand at 30 June 2026. Basis: calculation C1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 11–16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_krmn-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29

fields.value: The debt structure is known only through the company's own summaries. fields.value: The latest evidence is the second-quarter 2026 report. Two events after the quarter end appear in it only as short disclosures: the 20 July 2026 agreement to buy Walker Precision Engineering for about USD 94.0 million, expected to close in the third quarter, and the 3 August 2026 amendment that cut the term loan margin by 50 bp. Whether the acquisition closed, how it was funded and what the third quarter produced are not established.

Total term loan principal after the February 2026 repricing is USD 767.8 million in the annual report and USD 772 million in the quarterly reports; the revolver maturity is printed as 1 April 2030 in one place and 30 April 2030 in another; and the Seemann Composites acquisition is dated 3 February 2026 in the filings but January 2026 in the March and May 2026 releases. fields.value: The strongest case for higher readiness is that the filings agree with themselves on the figures that drive leverage and liquidity: the debt note ties to the balance sheet at year-end 2025 and at June 2026, and the quarterly chains tie to the annual totals. That case does not reach covenant headroom, guarantor and collateral coverage or anything after June 2026, which the filings cannot settle. Readiness would rise with the credit agreement and amendments, the third-quarter 2026 report and a report on the Walker closing and funding. It would fall if the third-quarter report restated earlier periods or revised the Seemann purchase accounting again, or if the credit agreement defined the covenant differently from the filings' summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Karman's leverage rose to 4.79x reported EBITDA at 30 June 2026 from 4.17x at year-end 2025 because acquisition debt arrived before the acquired earnings and operating cash flow was negative in 2025 and in the first half of 2026. Deleveraging therefore rests on earnings growth and backlog conversion, not on cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen on every measure. Total debt over reported EBITDA was 3.66x at year-end 2024, 4.17x at year-end 2025 and 4.79x on the twelve months to 30 June 2026, and net of cash it was 3.55x, 3.88x and 4.47x. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, net leverage was 3.27x, 3.20x and 3.94x. Pro forma for the Seemann cash paid on 3 February 2026, year-end 2025 net leverage would have been 5.63x on reported EBITDA. Total debt grew by USD 257,789 thousand in the first half of 2026, driven by a USD 265.0 million term loan increase that funded the Seemann acquisition, while the earnings base holds the acquired business only from 3 February 2026. The company states no pro forma EBITDA, so the 30 June 2026 ratio overstates run-rate leverage by an amount that is not established, and the only financial covenant, a springing test that applies when revolver loans exceed a threshold the filings do not state, was not required because the revolver was undrawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not support deleveraging yet. Operating cash flow was negative at USD 22,119 thousand in 2025 and negative at USD 2,975 thousand in the first half of 2026, although adjusted EBITDA was USD 145,302 thousand in 2025, mainly because contract assets absorbed cash: they rose USD 49,076 thousand in 2025 and stood at USD 187,120 thousand at 30 June 2026. After capital expenditure, free cash flow was negative at USD 42,455 thousand in 2025 and negative at USD 24,840 thousand in the first half of 2026, so the cash shortfall and the acquisitions were funded by borrowing and, in 2025, by equity. Contract liabilities, the customer advances that fund part of working capital, were USD 22,814 thousand at year-end 2025 against USD 29,868 thousand a year earlier, a smaller float from customers.

fields.value: The strongest contrary case is that the rise in leverage is timing: the Seemann debt was raised in February 2026 while its earnings are in the base for only part of the period, the adjusted EBITDA margin has stayed near 30%, backlog reached USD 1.3 billion at 30 June 2026 from USD 801,056 thousand at year-end 2025, and net leverage on adjusted EBITDA is 3.94x. That case wins if pro forma earnings show net leverage falling toward the year-end level and if contract assets stop growing so that operating cash flow turns positive after capital expenditure. It loses if working capital keeps absorbing cash, if the Walker acquisition adds debt before earnings, or if the credit agreement's covenant definition proves tighter than the filings' summary.

fields.value: Karman Holdings Inc. (krmn), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot (Full credit assessment). Scope: business, ownership, operating model, issuer history and governance behavior from the supplied annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases. No credit recommendation is made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Karman is a sole- and single-source supplier to missile and space programs with a growing backlog, but three customers supply about half of revenue, acquisitions are debt-funded and internal control weaknesses remain, so governance risk is medium and provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No document names who controls the company, so the view rests on issuer behavior: no dividend is planned, lenders cut the term loan margin twice, and a rising term loan funded four acquisitions since April 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand visibility is strong but concentrated in a few prime contractors. The company holds sole- or single-source positions on many programs and estimates that no single program exceeded 12% of revenue in 2025, yet three customers supplied 51.5% of revenue in 2025 and two held 40.7% of receivables at year-end 2025. In the first half of 2026 two customers were above 10% of revenue and held 29.7% of receivables at 30 June 2026. A delay or loss at one prime would hit earnings and cash collection together. Backlog, the value of existing contracts less amounts already invoiced, rose to USD 1.3 billion at 30 June 2026 from USD 801,056 thousand at year-end 2025, which supports 2026 revenue, although the U.S. government may terminate contracts at its convenience.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition program is the main driver of governance risk. Four acquisitions since April 2025 carried a combined fair value of consideration of USD 470,428 thousand and were funded by term loan increases, with some shares; a fifth, Walker, was agreed in July 2026 for about USD 94.0 million. The term loan started at USD 300.0 million and was raised by USD 75.0 million, USD 130.0 million and USD 265.0 million, and USD 764.0 million was outstanding at 30 June 2026. Debt arrives before acquired earnings, and integration costs are added back to adjusted EBITDA, so leverage tolerance is high. Seemann contributed USD 63.0 million of revenue in the first half of 2026, 18.90% of the total, but no pro forma earnings are given for any acquisition, so payback cannot be tested.

fields.value: The record on distributions and lender treatment is creditor-friendly so far. No dividend or fee to owners is documented, the company expects to retain earnings, and lenders accepted margin cuts of 75 bp in February 2026 and 50 bp in August 2026 and a revolver of USD 150.0 million. The secondary offerings in July 2025 and May 2026, priced at USD 49.00 and USD 61.00 a share, were sales by existing stockholders with no proceeds to the company, so they changed holder liquidity but not the capital structure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting controls are a clear governance weakness. Management reports that internal control over financial reporting was not effective at year-end 2025 and that disclosure controls were not effective at 30 June 2026 because of the same material weaknesses, which led to material adjustments to share-based compensation in 2023 and immaterial ones in 2025 and in the first half of 2026. The company says its information technology controls work is complete and the other remediation is still being implemented and tested, and the Seemann purchase price allocation was revised in the second quarter. The audit opinion on the statements is unqualified and gives no view on internal control, so lenders should treat interim figures as provisional until remediation is tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Who controls Karman is not established. The documents describe a classified board whose directors can be removed only for cause by a supermajority, a stockholder rights agreement and a registration rights agreement with certain investors, and unnamed selling stockholders, but they give no holdings, board seats or consent rights. The chief executive changed on 23 March 2026. Without the stockholder agreement and the proxy statement, sponsor willingness and capacity to extract value cannot be assessed, so the risk level rests on issuer behavior alone and is provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating pressure points are fixed-price exposure and working capital. Multi-year fixed-price contracts leave cost overruns with the company, contract assets rose USD 49,076 thousand in 2025 and absorbed operating cash, and capital expenditure of USD 21,865 thousand in the first half of 2026 was 6.56% of revenue against 4.31% in 2025. Growth is therefore consuming cash ahead of billing while debt has funded the acquisitions.

fields.value: The strongest case for lower risk is the behavior record: no distributions or fees to owners are documented, lenders accepted two margin cuts and a larger revolver, equity was raised at the initial public offering, none of the documents describes an amendment or exchange that disadvantages lenders, and backlog reached USD 1.3 billion. That case wins if the proxy statement and stockholder agreements show no controlling holder with extraction incentives and if pro forma earnings show the acquired businesses covering the new debt. The case for higher risk wins if the stockholder agreements give a holder control over financing, if the Walker acquisition is funded with further term loan before earnings, or if the control weaknesses lead to restated figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Karman is a high-growth, sole-source defense and space supplier whose credit quality is constrained by acquisition-funded leverage and negative free cash flow, so creditors depend on earnings growth, not cash generation, to bring leverage down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is average to strong, because sole- and single-source positions on long-lived programs and a rising order book give revenue visibility. Revenue grew 36.57% in 2025 and 54.85% in the first half of 2026, the company puts second-quarter organic growth at 24.4% without defining it, and backlog rose from USD 801,056 thousand at year-end 2025 to USD 1.3 billion at 30 June 2026. Programs can run for more than 20 years and the company says customers rarely requalify a supplier, so contracted work should convert into earnings that service debt, but the government may terminate contracts and its contracts are generally not fully funded at inception, so backlog measures visibility and not cash, and the company dropped the word funded from its backlog label in 2025 without restating amounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are stable on the company's adjusted measure and thinner on reported earnings, so leverage should be sized on the reported figure. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 29.16% in 2023, 30.74% in 2024, 30.82% in 2025 and 29.82% in the first half of 2026 against 30.48% a year earlier, while reported EBITDA margin was 27.16%, 28.39%, 25.41% and 26.30%. Add-backs of USD 25,476 thousand in 2025 were 17.53% of adjusted EBITDA and mostly acquisition costs and share-based compensation, and integration costs are still added back, so the adjusted margin is a less conservative measure of recurring cash earnings while the acquisition program continues. Gross margin rose from 37.60% in 2023 to 40.30% in 2025 and 42.64% in the first half of 2026, the clearest sign of operating leverage.

fields.value: Cash conversion is the weakest dimension, because EBITDA is not yet turning into free cash flow. Operating cash flow was negative USD 22,119 thousand in 2025 and negative USD 2,975 thousand in the first half of 2026, and free cash flow after capital expenditure, positive USD 11,393 thousand in 2024, was negative USD 42,455 thousand in 2025 and negative USD 24,840 thousand in the first half of 2026, a smaller outflow than the negative USD 39,624 thousand of the first half of 2025 and negative USD 27,671 thousand over the twelve months to 30 June 2026. Growth absorbs cash before it is billed: in the first half of 2026 receivables took USD 25,455 thousand and contract assets USD 24,851 thousand, and capital expenditure rose from 4.31% of revenue in 2025 to 6.56%. Debt, not cash flow, has therefore funded the acquisitions and the shortfall, and deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth and on working capital turning.

fields.value: Leverage is high for a company with negative free cash flow and was built faster than earnings. Net debt was USD 705,196 thousand at 30 June 2026, 4.47x reported EBITDA and 3.94x adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months, and finance leases of USD 102,139 thousand outside those figures take net leverage to 5.11x. Year-end 2025 net leverage was 3.88x on net debt of USD 465,189 thousand and, pro forma for the Seemann acquisition paid for on 3 February 2026, USD 675,189 thousand and 5.63x on earnings that hold none of the acquired business. If the 2026 outlook of USD 215.0 million to USD 222.5 million of adjusted EBITDA is met and net debt does not rise, net leverage would be 3.22x on that measure, but the outlook excludes any future acquisition.

Only scheduled amortization falls due before the revolver matures in 2030 and the term loan on 1 April 2032, the term loan bore 6.46% at 30 June 2026, and the August 2026 amendment lowers the margin by 50 bp, worth about USD 3,820 thousand a year and lifting cash interest cover from 2.97x to 3.20x. fields.value: The sector backdrop supports demand but concentrates risk in U.S. government budgets. Management points to more than USD 90 billion of recent prime-contractor awards for interceptors and over USD 76 billion for submarines, and the annual report says its proven missile-defense programs are positioned to feed the Golden Dome program, yet it also warns of shutdowns and continuing resolutions, tariffs and tight skilled labor. fields.value: The strongest evidence against a constrained view is that growth, margins and visibility are improving together: second-quarter organic growth was 24.4% by the company's account, adjusted EBITDA margin has held near 30%, the free cash outflow of the first half of 2026 was smaller than a year earlier, the 2026 outlook was raised in March, May and August 2026, and the backlog of USD 1.3 billion is about 2.21x twelve-month revenue. If the outlook is met and net debt stays at its June level, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA would fall to 3.22x, the repricing already lowers interest by about USD 3,820 thousand a year, and liquidity covers 4.06 years of the current cash outflow. The view would improve if operating cash flow turns positive after capital expenditure, if contract assets stop growing faster than revenue, if pro forma earnings show the acquired businesses covering their debt, and if the control weaknesses are reported as remediated. It would worsen if the Walker acquisition is funded with revolver or term loan before earnings, if a top-three customer delays or loses a program, if the revolver is drawn above the covenant test threshold, or if restated figures follow from the control weaknesses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Karman Holdings Inc. designs, tests and manufactures payload protection, aerodynamic interstage and propulsion systems for missile defense, tactical missile and space launch programs and sells mainly to prime contractors. Revenue was USD 471,500 thousand in 2025, split 31.81%, 31.78% and 36.41% across hypersonics and strategic missile defense, space and launch, and tactical missiles and integrated defense systems, and the maritime end market opened in 2026 with the Seemann acquisition. The company has grown through nine acquisitions since formation, selecting engineered products with intellectual property that can be used across programs, and it leases all of its facilities, so growth needs capital spending and lease capacity while the programs it serves are long-lived and recurring. The credit linkage is positive for cash-flow visibility and negative for liquidity preservation, because contract assets, fixed-price work and debt-funded acquisitions absorb the cash that the visibility should produce.

fields.value: Revenue is driven by production volumes on missile, interceptor and launch programs, by new content on existing programs and by acquisitions, with the company reporting second-quarter 2026 organic growth of 24.4% against total growth of 58.18%. Pricing power is therefore moderate: the company can defend its sole-source positions but cannot assume price increases, which supports stable gross margins but not margin expansion beyond operating leverage. For creditors this means revenue is durable in volume terms and exposed in timing and cost terms.

Operating cash flow over reported EBITDA was -18.46% in 2025 and 3.71% over the twelve months to 30 June 2026, and free cash flow was negative USD 27,671 thousand, so EBITDA does not yet translate into free cash flow for debt reduction or liquidity. Capital expenditure is a lever management has, but it has been rising, so FCF durability is weak.

fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: the supplier base is large and fragmented in piece parts and subsystems, with few integrated system providers, so the company competes mainly on technical content and integrated delivery, which holds prices but leaves the company exposed to the few integrated competitors. The company says the threat of new entrants is low because qualification is lengthy, programs run for decades and it holds intellectual property, which would protect revenue and support debt service if borne out. The threat of substitutes comes from customers bringing design and manufacture in-house or from government release of technical data, which would cut volumes at the primes' discretion. Buyer power is high: three customers supply 51.5% of revenue, the government can terminate contracts at its convenience and contracts are not fully funded at inception, so pricing and timing terms favor buyers. Supplier power is moderate: some components are sole-sourced and one supplier held 23.8% of payables at year-end 2025 and 12.0% at 31 March 2026, which can delay deliveries and raise cost.

fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material: the budget process has repeatedly ended in shutdowns and continuing resolutions that hold agencies to prior-year funding, and tariff rules were unsettled after the Supreme Court invalidated a significant portion of the tariffs in February 2026, which could raise costs that cannot be passed through. Economic factors are material through interest rates, because the term loan floats and carried 6.46% at 30 June 2026, and through the tight market for skilled labor. Social and technological factors are secondary to the credit case: hypersonics and missile defense programs are a source of demand, not of disruption. Political and economic factors therefore affect cash timing and interest cost more than they affect the demand case.

Weaknesses are net leverage of 4.47x, negative free cash flow, customer concentration of 51.5% in three customers and controls that are not effective. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the raised 2026 outlook converting into the 3.22x outlook-implied leverage, the August 2026 repricing, and prime awards for interceptors and submarines that management cites. fields.value: Scale and market position are average: revenue of USD 471,500 thousand in 2025 supports a niche position in subsystems, but market share is not given and the market-leading claim is management's own. Competitive advantage is strong on documented sole-source and long-program positions, though customers hold bargaining power. Business diversification is average: three balanced end markets and no program above 12% of revenue, offset by 51.5% of revenue in three customers and one budget source. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital expenditure is rising to 6.56% of revenue and fixed-price work limits cost relief. Margin stability is average, strong only on the adjusted basis. Free cash flow stability is weak, at negative USD 27,671 thousand over the twelve months. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the company completed an initial public offering and two secondary sales, lenders repriced twice and upsized the revolver, but there is no rating or traded debt in the documents and net leverage is 4.47x. Liquidity is average, because 74.35% of it is the revolver and the Walker acquisition is pending. Financial policy and governance are weak for now, given acquisition-funded leverage, no stated leverage target, ineffective controls and an unidentified controlling holder. The trend is improving in earnings and in the free cash outflow, which narrowed in the first half of 2026, and worsening in leverage, and the missing data are pro forma earnings, the credit agreement, ownership and third-quarter 2026 results.

fields.value: The most credible downside starts with a delay, de-scoping or cost overrun on a program at one of the three customers that supply 51.5% of revenue, or with a budget disruption that holds new awards, in a year when the Walker acquisition closes. Revenue and fixed-cost absorption weaken first, contract assets and receivables then build further because the two customers above 10% of revenue hold 29.7% of receivables, and free cash flow, already negative USD 24,840 thousand in the first half of 2026, worsens. If the shortfall and Walker were funded from the revolver, which is 74.35% of USD 201,741 thousand of liquidity, leverage would rise from 4.47x and the 6.50x first-lien net leverage test would come into effect once the draw passes the unstated threshold. Interest on the floating term loan costs USD 7,640 thousand a year for each 100 bp, and no bullet maturity falls due before 2030, so distress within twelve months is unlikely: liquidity equals 4.06 years of the current outflow. Management can cut capital expenditure, pause acquisitions and withhold dividends, and equity markets were open at USD 61.00 a share in May 2026; the first observable signs would be a falling backlog, rising contract assets and revolver draws.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Karman presents an adequate business profile supported by sole-source positions, a backlog of USD 1.3 billion and adjusted EBITDA margin near 30%, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-funded net leverage of 4.47x, negative free cash flow and control weaknesses that are not remediated. Cash-flow durability appears weak because working capital and capital expenditure absorb the cash that EBITDA produces. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA growth reaching the outlook, on the revolver staying available and on the interest rate, with no bullet maturity before 2030. The primary downside path is a customer or budget disruption during a debt-funded acquisition, which would raise revolver use and leverage before earnings catch up. Further analysis would require pro forma earnings, the credit agreement, ownership and the third-quarter 2026 results. Top risk: acquisition-funded leverage without free cash flow.
